sentences.text: Indore, Dated : 29.01.2020 :-
Shri R.R.Bhatnagar, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Vikas Yadav, learned Public Prosecutor for the Respondent/State.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant on the question of admission.
The revision seems to be arguable, therefore, admitted for final hearing.
No notice is necessary as Public Prosecutor accepted the notice.
Also heard on IA No.7781/2019, which is first application for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant - Sanjay.

The applicant has been convicted for offence under Section 7 (1) read with Section 16 (1) (A) (1) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentenced to undergo 1 year RI with fine of Rs.2,000/-,
with default stipulation.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant was on bail during trial and he has never misused the liberty so granted to him.
However, subject to final outcome of this revision, jail sentence of the applicant may be ordered to be suspended.
After having perused the impugned judgment and on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, IA No.7781/2019 is allowed.

The substantive jail sentence of applicant - Sanjay is suspended subject to his depositing the fine amount and furnishing a personal bond in the sum -: 2 :- Criminal Revision No.4670 of 2019.
of Rs.50,000-00 [Fifty Thousand Rupees] with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 08.12.2020 and Sanjay vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh Thr. ... on 29 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14245877/
